description: Local defensive hardening snippets for owner-authorized server inventory enrichment. This catalog intentionally excludes malware samples, exploit code, payloads, offensive procedures, credentials, target lists, and proof-of-concept material.

artifacts.title: Remote Administration Access Hardening
artifacts.summary: Review exposed SSH, RDP, WinRM, VNC, and similar remote administration services.
artifacts.match_rationale: Remote administration services deserve tight exposure, authentication, and monitoring controls.
artifacts.snippet: Remote administration services should be reachable only from approved management paths such as a VPN, bastion, or restricted administrative network. Require phishing-resistant MFA where feasible, disable password-only access where policy allows, remove stale local and domain accounts, and log successful and failed access attempts. Confirm the service is still required, patched through the vendor or OS package channel, and covered by alerting for unusual source locations, new administrators, and repeated failed authentication.

artifacts.title: Web Service Hardening Review
artifacts.summary: Review exposed HTTP, HTTPS, reverse proxy, and application server surfaces.
artifacts.match_rationale: Web services are common internet-facing entry points and need baseline hardening even when the detected version is current.
artifacts.snippet: Confirm the web service is intentionally exposed and fronted by the expected reverse proxy, load balancer, or application gateway. Remove default sites, sample applications, unused modules, and stale virtual hosts. Verify TLS is enforced for authenticated or sensitive traffic, patch through the vendor or OS package channel, and make sure access logs are retained. Review whether admin consoles, debug endpoints, metrics, and backup files are blocked from untrusted networks.

artifacts.title: TLS Certificate And Cipher Baseline
artifacts.summary: Review encrypted services for certificate validity and modern TLS configuration.
artifacts.match_rationale: Encrypted services still need certificate lifecycle, protocol, and cipher review.
artifacts.snippet: Check that certificates are valid, trusted by expected clients, named correctly, and monitored before expiration. Disable legacy protocol versions and weak cipher suites according to your platform baseline. Confirm certificate private keys are protected, renewal is automated or tracked, and service owners know which load balancers, proxies, and application servers terminate TLS.

artifacts.title: Database Exposure Hardening
artifacts.summary: Review database listeners for network reachability, authentication, patching, and logging.
artifacts.match_rationale: Database services should usually be private, tightly authenticated, and monitored.
artifacts.snippet: Confirm the database listener is not exposed beyond the application or administration networks that need it. Require strong authentication, remove default or stale accounts, and enforce encryption where supported. Verify backups are protected and tested, audit logging is enabled for privileged actions, and patching follows the vendor or managed-service maintenance path. For cache and search services, confirm unauthenticated or anonymous access is disabled.

artifacts.title: Legacy Or Cleartext Service Retirement
artifacts.summary: Review FTP, Telnet, cleartext mail protocols, and other legacy services for replacement or isolation.
artifacts.match_rationale: Legacy or cleartext services can expose credentials and should be retired, wrapped, or isolated.
artifacts.snippet: Identify the business owner and confirm whether the legacy service is still needed. Prefer modern encrypted replacements such as SFTP, SSH, HTTPS, IMAPS, or authenticated relay designs. If retirement is not immediately possible, restrict source networks, prevent credential reuse, monitor use, and document a time-bound exception with compensating controls.

artifacts.title: SMB And File Sharing Hardening
artifacts.summary: Review SMB and file sharing services for exposure, signing, access control, and backup coverage.
artifacts.match_rationale: File sharing services often carry sensitive data and lateral-movement risk if broadly reachable.
artifacts.snippet: Confirm SMB is only reachable from trusted internal networks and not from the public internet. Disable unsupported protocol versions, require signing where your environment supports it, and review share permissions for least privilege. Monitor privileged file access, verify endpoint and server patching, and ensure critical shares are included in offline or immutable backup coverage.

artifacts.title: Linux Package Backport Version Check
artifacts.summary: Treat older-looking Linux service banners as leads until package-level vendor support is checked.
artifacts.match_rationale: Linux distributions often backport security fixes while retaining older upstream version strings.
artifacts.snippet: Do not treat the banner version alone as proof of vulnerability. Check the OS distribution, package name, package release, and vendor security advisory status. Record whether the package is supported, whether security updates are enabled, and whether the host is receiving updates from the expected repository or management system.

artifacts.title: Windows Server Role Hardening
artifacts.summary: Review Windows server roles for patching, privileged access, logging, and exposed management paths.
artifacts.match_rationale: Windows server roles need patching, role minimization, privileged-access controls, and event visibility.
artifacts.snippet: Verify the host is enrolled in patch management and that only required Windows roles and features are enabled. Restrict RDP and WinRM to approved administration paths, use separate privileged accounts, and review local Administrators group membership. Confirm event forwarding or centralized logging covers authentication, service changes, new local accounts, and privilege changes.

artifacts.title: DNS Service Hardening Review
artifacts.summary: Review DNS listeners for recursion policy, zone-transfer controls, logging, and patching.
artifacts.match_rationale: DNS services affect availability, name resolution integrity, and exposure to abuse if recursion or transfers are misconfigured.
artifacts.snippet: Confirm whether the DNS service is authoritative, recursive, forwarding, or internal-only. Restrict recursion to approved clients, limit zone transfers to authorized peers, and review split-horizon boundaries. Verify logging covers query volume and administrative changes, patch through the vendor or OS package channel, and confirm secondary DNS or resolver failover is documented.

artifacts.title: Mail Service Relay And Mailbox Hardening
artifacts.summary: Review SMTP, submission, POP, IMAP, and mail gateway services for relay, authentication, TLS, and logging controls.
artifacts.match_rationale: Mail services need relay restrictions, strong authentication, TLS policy, abuse monitoring, and backup delivery planning.
artifacts.snippet: Confirm SMTP relay is restricted to approved sources and that mailbox access requires strong authentication. Prefer encrypted submission and mailbox protocols, remove legacy cleartext access where possible, and monitor authentication failures, relay attempts, queue growth, and unusual sending patterns. Review SPF, DKIM, and DMARC ownership where applicable, and verify patching, backups, and abuse-response contacts are current.

artifacts.title: Identity And Directory Service Hardening
artifacts.summary: Review LDAP, Kerberos, directory, and domain-controller surfaces for exposure, privileged access, and logging.
artifacts.match_rationale: Identity services are high-impact control-plane systems and should be tightly scoped, monitored, and backed up.
artifacts.snippet: Confirm directory and Kerberos services are reachable only from intended networks and administrative paths. Review privileged groups, service accounts, stale accounts, password and MFA policy, and secure LDAP or equivalent protections where supported. Ensure logs cover authentication, directory changes, privilege changes, replication health, and new trust relationships. Verify authoritative backups and recovery procedures are tested.

artifacts.title: VPN And Edge Access Hardening
artifacts.summary: Review VPN and edge access services for MFA, patching, source restrictions, and session monitoring.
artifacts.match_rationale: VPN and edge access services are common control points for remote administration and workforce access.
artifacts.snippet: Confirm the edge access service is still required, patched, and covered by vendor security advisories. Require MFA for interactive access, remove stale users and device profiles, and restrict administrative interfaces to approved management paths. Monitor new logins, unusual geographies, failed authentication spikes, configuration changes, and session duration anomalies. Document emergency access and recovery procedures separately from routine user access.

artifacts.title: Container And Orchestration Admin Surface Review
artifacts.summary: Review Docker, Kubernetes, kubelet, and etcd surfaces for authenticated administration and network exposure.
artifacts.match_rationale: Container control-plane and runtime APIs can carry high operational impact if exposed or weakly authenticated.
artifacts.snippet: Confirm container runtime, orchestration, and key-value store APIs are not reachable from untrusted networks. Require authenticated and encrypted administration, rotate stale credentials or tokens, and review role bindings for least privilege. Verify control-plane audit logs, admission controls, image provenance checks, backup coverage for cluster state, and patch cadence for nodes and control-plane components.

artifacts.title: Monitoring And Observability Admin Surface Review
artifacts.summary: Review monitoring, dashboard, metrics, and log-search services for exposure, authentication, and data sensitivity.
artifacts.match_rationale: Monitoring tools can expose sensitive operational data and privileged administrative controls.
artifacts.snippet: Confirm dashboards, metrics endpoints, and log-search interfaces require authentication and are reachable only from intended networks. Review admin users, API tokens, data-source credentials, alert routing, and public sharing settings. Check whether collected logs or metrics expose sensitive hostnames, internal paths, secrets, or security events, and verify backup and recovery for alerting rules and dashboard configuration.

artifacts.title: Known Exploited Vulnerability Triage
artifacts.summary: Prioritize lifecycle findings against CISA KEV and vendor advisories before deciding remediation order.
artifacts.match_rationale: Versioned services and lifecycle findings should be checked against known exploited vulnerability and vendor advisory sources.
artifacts.snippet: Use the detected product, version, CPE, and vendor package metadata to check whether the asset maps to a known exploited vulnerability or urgent vendor advisory. Record the source, advisory identifier, due date if applicable, and remediation owner. If the version appears old but the vendor backports fixes, document the package release evidence instead of relying on the banner alone.

artifacts.title: General Service Inventory Review
artifacts.summary: Fallback defensive review for inventory rows that do not match a more specific artifact.
artifacts.match_rationale: Fallback item assigned so every server CSV row has at least one defensive reference.
artifacts.snippet: Confirm the service is expected, owned, patched, monitored, backed up where applicable, and reachable only from intended networks. Record the asset owner, business purpose, patch source, authentication model, logging location, and retirement plan if the service is no longer required. Treat this item as a prompt for manual review, not as proof of vulnerability.
